channel.title: Pass the Architect: CCAR-F retake
channel.description: A two-host study series for resitting the Claude Certified Architect - Foundations exam: the thirty task statements, the six scenarios, and the miss patterns that cost marks.
channel.itunes:summary: A two-host study series for resitting the Claude Certified Architect - Foundations exam: the thirty task statements, the six scenarios, and the miss patterns that cost marks.
channel.itunes:author: Pass the Architect

item.title: 12. Foundations final drill
item.description: About forty rapid-fire items across the five Foundations domains, weighted by the blueprint and by the last attempt's gaps, each set in one of the six scenarios, then the guide's named anti-patterns and a calm walk through exam day.

item.title: 11. The six scenarios
item.description: All six Foundations scenarios in the exam guide's order: the system, its primary domains, the three decisions the exam keeps probing, the classic trap, an argued distractor and a drill for each, then the patterns that run through all six.

item.title: 10. Closing the Foundations Gaps
item.description: A bonus episode on the applied configuration and API mechanics that both Architect exams test inside their scenarios: enforcement versus guidance, settings and M C P scope, tool sequencing, the agentic loop, extraction schemas, review routing and feedback loops.

item.title: 09. Context, review and provenance
item.description: Keeping exact facts alive through long sessions, exploring large codebases without context degradation, routing extractions to human review by calibrated confidence and stratified sampling, and carrying sources and conflicts intact through multi-agent synthesis.

item.title: 08. Tool design and built-in tools
item.description: How Claude picks a tool, how a tool should fail, how many tools each agent should hold, and which built-in tool fits which job: task statements 2.1, 2.2, 2.3 and 2.5, drilled in the customer support and developer productivity scenarios.

item.title: 07. Hooks, sessions and escalation
item.description: Agent SDK hooks that block, redirect and normalise; when to resume, fork or start fresh with a summary; and the escalation triggers the exam trusts versus the ones it calls unreliable.

item.title: 06. Coordinators, subagents and decomposition
item.description: How a coordinator runs a team of subagents: hub-and-spoke routing, isolated subagent context and explicit context passing, the Task tool and parallel spawning, scoped subagent tools, coverage loops, and when to pick a fixed pipeline over dynamic decomposition.

item.title: 05. The agentic loop and enforced workflows
item.description: Stop reasons, appending tool results to a stateless API, forced tool choice for first calls, programmatic prerequisites, structured handoffs, and how errors should travel between agents. Drilled in the customer support and multi-agent research scenarios.

item.title: 04. Prompts and structured output
item.description: Explicit review criteria, few-shot examples, tool use with JSON schemas and tool choice, validation and retry loops, the Message Batches API, and independent review passes, drilled inside the extraction and continuous integration scenarios.

item.title: 03. Plan mode, refinement and CI
item.description: When to plan and when to just make the change, how to steer Claude Code with examples, tests and targeted feedback, and how to run it in a CI pipeline that posts clean, non-duplicated, low-noise review comments.

item.title: 02. Claude Code configuration
item.description: Where each instruction lives in Claude Code and who receives it: the CLAUDE dot md hierarchy, imports and rules files, project and personal commands and skills, path-scoped rules, and M C P servers at project and user scope.

item.title: 01. Your Five Miss Patterns
item.description: A bonus episode on the five answering habits that cost marks at Foundations, with a one-line self-check and a trap-built drill for each, the guide's thesis, and a pacing plan for the Pearson VUE interface.

item.title: 00. Foundations game plan
item.description: How the Foundations exam is built: sixty items across four of six scenarios, the domain weights, a pacing plan for the Pearson VUE screen, and a four-step method worked through three official sample questions.
